note: Attacker-controlled length is multiplied by byte_mul without an overflow check, unlike ndr_pull_charset which checks length > UINT32_MAX/byte_mul. A crafted length such that length*byte_mul wraps to a small value bypasses the buffer-size check.
The wrapped small value passes NDR_PULL_NEED_BYTES, so the parser proceeds even though the actual required bytes exceed the remaining input buffer.
ndr_string_length scans the input buffer for a terminator; because the buffer-size check was bypassed, it reads past the end of the allocated input buffer.
The MIN with the attacker-controlled length does not prevent the out-of-bounds read performed by ndr_string_length in the previous step.
The parser advances the offset past the end of the input buffer, leading to an out-of-bounds read/write in subsequent parsing operations.
